$comment: CANONICAL CURRENT-STATE RECORD — the single source of truth for hosted migration state.
Repository state (repo max, next free number, totals) is DERIVED from supabase/migrations/*.sql
by scripts/migration-state.mjs and must never be written here or duplicated in docs.
Hosted state cannot be derived from filenames, so it is declared here ONCE and referenced
everywhere else. Update this file in the same change that records a production apply.
hosted_applied_at_precision: DATE-ONLY, AND DELIBERATELY SO. NO EXACT APPLY TIMESTAMP WAS CAPTURED FOR 0182, AND NONE IS INVENTED. Unlike 0177–0181, whose hosted_applied_at values are observed CLIENT-SIDE apply markers read off the operator console, the 0182 apply was reported to the repository as text with no clock reading attached, and it was performed on a machine this repository has no telemetry from. Read the value above as the CALENDAR DATE ONLY — the hours, minutes and seconds are NOT KNOWN, and a parser that renders it as 2026-08-16T00:00:00Z is reading precision that does not exist. What IS provable, repository-side: the apply preceded the merge commit bf1b18a920b5a1d0ddb10910335a865e96aa61bf, whose committer date is 2026-08-16T15:08:27Z, because the rollout was migration-first and the post-apply migration list was reported before that merge. A narrower bracket (after 2026-08-16T14:12:22Z, when the release run stopped at the credential boundary with 0182 still unapplied; before 2026-08-16T15:07:24Z, when the completed apply was reported) comes from the operator host’s release-session record, which is NOT a repository artifact and is cited in the ledger as such rather than promoted to a precise value here. NOTE ALSO that no server-side apply timestamp exists for ANY migration: supabase_migrations.schema_migrations has no timestamp column.
hosted_note: 0182_sterile_item_discard_lifecycle.sql APPLIED to production on 2026-08-16, MIGRATION-FIRST, from the authorized #590 head c020e1022b585daecdb2ef5ad7784e987c2fbb3d (project alhhybgqdmcdyzpybykj, Supabase CLI 2.102.0), raw sha256 07ee23e1254329168e205f42b47c351205ebb306afc0f7d524b69c8d14ecda57, executable sha256 799690db5fba3a4c24d0c100384784344a5b6c14c5d83a4eeec4e9418fba8fba. WHO APPLIED IT, AND FROM WHERE — THIS BOUNDS EVERY EVIDENCE LINE BELOW: the credentialed step was performed BY THE OPERATOR on his own authorized machine, NOT from the repository host. No Supabase production credential was ever present on the repository host, and the production database password was removed from the operator shell after use. Every apply observation recorded here is therefore an OPERATOR-REPORTED CONSOLE OBSERVATION transcribed verbatim — it is NOT a measurement taken by this repository, by CI, or by any automation in it. APPLY EXIT STATUS: PUSH EXIT CODE WAS NOT CAPTURED. No client process exit code for `supabase db push` was observed or recorded, and none is claimed, inferred or reconstructed. This is NOT the 0181 case, where exit 0 was deliberately captured by backgrounding the command; it is the 0180 situation — the push exit status is simply unknown, and is recorded as unknown. DRY RUN (immediately before the apply): proposed 0182_sterile_item_discard_lifecycle.sql AND NOTHING ELSE, and its DRY RUN EXIT CODE 0 WAS CAPTURED. That captured 0 belongs to the DRY RUN ONLY and must never be read as the push’s exit status. PRE-APPLY migration list: 0180 | 0180, 0181 | 0181, 0182 | <empty remote> — 0182 present locally, absent remotely. APPLY: the CLI prompted “Do you want to push these migrations to the remote database? 0182_sterile_item_discard_lifecycle.sql”, the operator confirmed, and the CLI then printed “Applying migration 0182_sterile_item_discard_lifecycle.sql...” followed by “Finished supabase db push.” POST-APPLY migration list: 0176 | 0176, 0177 | 0177, 0178 | 0178, 0179 | 0179, 0180 | 0180, 0181 | 0181, 0182 | 0182 — 0182 recorded LOCALLY AND REMOTELY; hosted migration history max is 0182. SCHEMA EVIDENCE: a successful production REMOTE SCHEMA DUMP shows public.record_keeping_sterile_items.date_discarded as `date_discarded date` — NULLABLE, NO DEFAULT — matching the reviewed migration and the record_keeping_disinfectants precedent (0085/0096) exactly. The other date_discarded in that dump is that pre-existing sibling column, not a second new one. EVIDENCE LIMITATIONS, STATED PLAINLY AND NOT PAPERED OVER. (a) NO PUSH EXIT CODE — see APPLY EXIT STATUS above. (b) NO ROW-COUNT PROOF: no pre/post business-row count was captured for any table, so NO zero-row-mutation claim is made FROM MEASUREMENT. What IS asserted is a claim about the migration TEXT, which any reader can re-check against the frozen bytes: 0182’s only executable statements are one `alter table public.record_keeping_sterile_items add column if not exists date_discarded date` and one `comment on column`, inside a single begin/commit — no UPDATE, no INSERT, no DELETE, no backfill, no index, no constraint, no policy, no grant, no trigger, no function and no view. That is pinned by tests/migrations/0182-sterile-item-discard-lifecycle.test.ts, which also pins the raw checksum above. (c) NO DIRECT SQL VERIFICATION: `supabase db query --linked` was UNAVAILABLE because the Management API returned 403, so the post-apply proof rests on the successful remote schema dump plus the remote migration list — not on an ad-hoc query. (d) NO EXACT APPLY TIMESTAMP — see hosted_applied_at and hosted_applied_at_precision. (e) NO SERVER-SIDE APPLY TIMESTAMP EXISTS AT ALL, for any migration: supabase_migrations.schema_migrations carries only (version, statements, name) and has no timestamp column, so no later archaeology can recover one. RELEASE: the production release was subsequently verified healthy. The application merge is bf1b18a920b5a1d0ddb10910335a865e96aa61bf (PR #590), a normal two-parent merge — parent 1 0943c31e9b35845b566f7dbae366746a66f650c0 = the previous production head, parent 2 c020e1022b585daecdb2ef5ad7784e987c2fbb3d = the authorized feature head. The DATABASE WAS APPLIED FIRST, before that merge. 0182 is purely additive and nullable, so OLD APP + NEW DB was safe throughout the window between the apply and the merge, and every pre-existing row arrived as date_discarded IS NULL, which is exactly “no structured discard recorded”. FINAL STATE: repository max 0182, hosted max 0182, repo == hosted, nothing pending, next free 0183 (AVAILABLE BUT NOT CLAIMED).
